text:
acme_oncall: Hey team — our batch rerank started returning scores that don't line up with candidates. looks like scores are shifted by one for queries that have an empty candidate list. reproducible and blocking prod traffic.

jess: sorry to hear that — can you paste a minimal request that reproduces it? also which API version + SDK?

acme_oncall: using /v1/rerank batch endpoint, Python SDK 0.8.2. minimal payload:
```json
{
  \"queries\": ["q1", "q2", "q3"],
  \"candidates\": [
    ["a","b"],
    [],
    ["c"]
  ]
}
```
response (trimmed):
```json
{
  \"scores\": [0.8, 0.1, 0.7]
}
```
expected: scores grouped per-query (2,0,1). actual: treated as [q1:0.8, q2:0.1] and q3 gets 0.7 but ordering is off when any inner list is empty.

mike: ack. can you share the exact HTTP payload (raw) and a request id? i want to repro locally.

acme_oncall: request-id: req_20240324_84
raw body is above. sending cURL now:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -H 'Authorization: Bearer xxxxxx' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @payload.json
```

olivia: digging into the client/server serialization — quick hypothesis: the server flattens candidates and uses a per-query counts vector. if counts vector is computed client-side incorrectly when an inner list is empty, offsets will shift. does your SDK version have a change in the batching logic?

acme_oncall: we didn't change our client. we recently switched to SDK 0.8.2 last week and started seeing it then.

sam: i can repro with a small test. running a unit with identical payload in local harness.

repro-bot: test run id t-4421 — reproduced. observed flattened_candidates.length == 3 but counts == [2,1,0] instead of [2,0,1].

mike: thanks — that points to counts being built by iterating candidate arrays and doing an inplace pop when empty. pushing a quick check into SDK and server.

jess: customer-facing note: workaround for now is to ensure you include an explicit empty placeholder candidate for queries that have zero real candidates, e.g. "" and ignore it client-side after reranking. i know it's ugly but it avoids offset collapse.

acme_oncall: can we get an ETA on a proper fix? this is affecting multiple customers.

mike: we traced it: Python SDK (0.8.2) introduced a change that reorders how candidates are serialized for compression; server expects counts to be computed prior to compression. root cause is SDK bug. patching SDK now and adding server-side verification to tolerate empty lists.

olivia: patch plan:
- SDK 0.8.3: restore stable counts computation + explicit counts header
- Server: defensive check to recompute counts when header mismatch and return 4xx with clear message if unrecoverable
- Add regression test covering various empty/varied candidate shapes

sam: QA will validate and run integration tests to ensure no perf regression.

jess: we pushed a temporary mitigation to prod: server now rejects mismatched counts with HTTP 400 + message guiding to SDK upgrade/workaround. that will stop silent misalignments.

mike: SDK 0.8.3 draft release: https://git.internal/redwood/sdk/commit/ab3f9e (patch adds explicit `candidates_counts` field). releasing hotfix to pip in ~40m.

acme_oncall: appreciated. we'll try the workaround for now and upgrade once you confirm the fix.

jess: once 0.8.3 is published i'll DM you the release notes + migration snippet. followup: add you to early rollout channel so we can monitor.

acme_oncall: thanks — adding logs and will report back after upgrade.

repro-bot: follow-up test after server reject rule: test id t-4422 — request rejected with 400 and message `counts-mismatch: expected counts header` (as intended).

mike: marking this as P1 and linking to internal jira REDINF-3129. ETA for full deployment: 24 hours.

olivia: note for release: include example of safe serialization:
```json
{
  "queries": ["q1","q2","q3"],
  "candidates": [["a","b"],[""],["c"]],
  "candidates_counts": [2,1,1]
}
```
server can ignore placeholder content but counts preserve offsets.

jess: closing loop: will update support ticket with workaround + ETA. thanks all :slightly_smiling_face:

acme_oncall: thanks team :pray:
